chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in the resting places of camels. He said: If you fear loss regarding your belongings, then sweep it, sprinkle it with water, and perform salat (prayer); and there is no objection to salat (prayer) in the sheepfolds.
So the proper understanding of this report is the state of necessity, in accordance with what the report contains of fear for one’s belongings or something similar.

key_terms.أَعْطَانِ الْإِبِلِ: the resting places or watering grounds of camels
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity, the condition qualifying the ruling
key_terms.الضَّيْعَةَ: loss or harm feared concerning one’s property
key_terms.فَاكْنُسْهُ: sweep it, meaning clean the place
key_terms.مَرَابِضِ الْغَنَمِ: the sheepfolds or resting places of sheep

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in the resting places of camels or in sheepfolds?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) in animal enclosures, especially the resting places of camels and the sheepfolds. It indicates that praying in such a place may be allowed in a state of necessity after cleaning and sprinkling the area, while prayer in sheepfolds is not problematic. The closing statement clarifies that the report is understood in the context of necessity.
